- When sentiment turns sharply negative (especially after a spike), model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast downward by 10–20% of the spike magnitude.
- If sentiment remains positive for 3+ consecutive days with high news volume, model often underestimates upward momentum — increase forecast by 5–15% of recent mean.
- After a strong upward spike in sentiment, model frequently overshoots in the next 3–5 days — apply a 5–10% downward correction to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly negative with high news volume, model often underestimates volatility — add 2–5% buffer to forecast range.
- Model tends to lag in mean reversion — if sentiment shows clear reversal, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect the trend shift.
- When sentiment is consistently low (0.0–0.33) for 5+ days, model underestimates downside risk — add 3–7% downward bias to forecast.
- If sentiment is high (0.67–1.00) and news volume is stable, model often overestimates short-term upside — reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
